tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	# Password credentials
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-10-22. **Status:** design approved in conversation; spec awaiting review.
4	**Base:** `origin/main` at `ce1e1088` (clean-room core merged in #1702).
5	**Builds on:** `2026-08-16-user-centric-credential-model-design.md` (sub-project C, never specced until now) and the 2026-09-16 multi-credential decisions (memory `project_multi_credential_types_plan`).
6	
7	## Goal
8	
9	A user can hold a password as well as, or instead of, a PIN. Lock Code Manager writes it to every lock in the entry that takes passwords and keeps it in sync there, the way it does PINs today.
10	
11	## Scope
12	
13	In:
14	
15	- Password as a second managed credential type, end to end: sync core, storage, Z-Wave and Virtual providers, entities, config, services, websocket, slot card, add-user card and lock card.
16	- Making the core type-generic, so that RFID and NFC can later be added as data, not as structure.
17	
18	Out:
19	
20	- RFID, NFC and biometrics.
21	- A pattern on the PIN entity (see "Text entities").
22	- Showing or editing unmanaged passwords on the lock card.
23	- User Code CC locks whose keypad accepts non-digit characters. The driver uses the Password type for these (`node-zwave-js AccessControl.ts:1598`), and they may be invisible to Lock Code Manager today. Follow-up issue.
24	
25	## Decisions
26	
27	| # | Decision |
28	|---|---|
29	| 1 | Passwords are printable ASCII, 0x20–0x7E, spaces included. The Z-Wave spec requires passwords to travel as UTF-16 big endian (CC:0083.01.0A.11.021) and counts Credential Length in bytes (.0A.11.014/.015). 2026A's worked example gives a 17-character password a length of 34. Every printable ASCII character is exactly 2 bytes, so the per-lock length check compares `2 × len(password)` against the lock's limits. |
30	| 2 | The sync core is keyed by `CredentialAddress(slot, type)`. There is still one worker per lock. |
31	| 3 | Release stays per slot: one release removes every type Lock Code Manager wrote for the slot. |
32	| 4 | A slot needs at least one credential of any type. Clearing a credential disables the slot only when no other credential remains. A stored value counts even if no current lock takes its type. |
33	| 5 | On Z-Wave, the password index is allocated by the provider: it finds the tagged user's password wherever it is, or else takes the lowest password index no user holds. PIN keeps following the slot. |
34	| 6 | Credential text entities set no `pattern`, `native_min` or `native_max`. One validator and the coordinator's per-lock length check are the only gates, and their errors never contain the value. |
35	| 7 | Passwords are not whitespace-stripped. PINs keep `vol.Strip`. |
36	| 8 | Slot card: tabs per type over one value field, each tab's dot showing that type's sync state. Tabs appear only when the entry offers more than one type. |
37	| 9 | Lock card: tabs per type. The PIN tab is today's card. The Password tab lists managed users' passwords on that lock. |
38	| 10 | Carried from 2026-09-16: an entry's available types are the union across its locks. A type no longer offered keeps its stored value, and its entity is removed. Per-type in-sync sensors are disabled by default. Duplicates are refused within a type and allowed across types. The generator covers passwords. |
39	
40	## Sync core
41	
42	`CredentialAddress(user_ref, credential_type)` already exists (`model/credentials.py`). It becomes the key everywhere in `sync/`:
43	
44	- `LockWorker.slots: dict[CredentialAddress, Slot]`. `want`, `forget`, `resume`, `status`, `syncing` and `push` take an address.
45	- `LockPort.read(addresses) -> Mapping[CredentialAddress, Reading]` and `LockPort.write(address, value) -> bool | None`.
46	- `sync/slot.py` stays a single-value state machine. `Holds.pin` becomes `Holds.value`, `Want` stays `str | None`, and `Holds.__repr__` keeps masking.
47	- `sync/registry.py` and `ha/adapter.py` re-key to match. The adapter turns an address into the provider call for that type.
48	- Release is per slot. When a slot leaves the entry, the worker sends one release for the slot. The provider removes every credential Lock Code Manager wrote to that slot's user, then the user only if it holds nothing else.
49	
50	**Managed addresses are per lock:** `{CredentialAddress(slot, t) for t in lock.capabilities.credential_types ∩ MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES}`. This covers every type the lock takes, not only the types the user has a value for. A user with no password still gets a password address on a password lock, with want `None`, so a password cleared or never set is kept cleared, the same way an empty PIN is kept cleared today. A lock that doesn't take password never gets a password address, so the aggregate `in_sync` on that lock ignores the type. This fixes the global `managed_addresses()` gap found in the #1572 review. Recompute when a lock is added or removed and when capabilities refresh.
51	
52	`MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES` becomes `{PIN, PASSWORD}`.
53	
54	## Storage
55	
56	`ha/lock_store.py`, `STORE_VERSION` 1 → 2.
57	
58	- v1 slot record: `{"wrote": <fingerprint|cleared>, …release fields}`.
59	- v2 slot record: `{"wrote": {"pin": <fingerprint|cleared>, "password": REDACTED, …release fields}`.
60	- Migration: move v1 `wrote` under `"pin"`. Release fields stay at slot level.
61	- The fingerprint covers the type: `fingerprint(type, value, salt)`. Credential values are never persisted.
62	
63	The Store migration is the only one-way step. Downgrading leaves a v2 Store the old version can't read, and HA's Store versioning is there to refuse that.
64	
65	## Configuration and the credential-required rule
66	
67	- The user subentry gets an optional `password` (absent means none), and setup YAML gets `password:` per user. No config-entry migration is needed.
68	- The rule changes in four places:
69	  - `ha/slot_coordinator.py:294`: clearing any credential disables an enabled slot only if no other credential remains.
70	  - `ha/slot_coordinator.py:355`: enabling is refused only when the user has no credential of any type. `PinRequiredError` becomes `CredentialRequiredError`.
71	  - `config_flow.py:84-93, 422`: `_slot_enabled_without_pin` becomes `_slot_enabled_without_credential`, which checks every managed type's field.
72	  - Repair `pin_required` becomes `credential_required`. Update `switch.py:62`, `ha/services.py:451`, `repairs.py:179` and `__init__.py:1220`. At startup, delete any leftover `pin_required_*` issue.
73	
74	## Providers
75	
76	**Z-Wave (`providers/zwave_js.py`)**
77

# Password credentials

**Date:** 2026-10-22. **Status:** design approved in conversation; spec awaiting review.
**Base:** `origin/main` at `ce1e1088` (clean-room core merged in #1702).
**Builds on:** `2026-08-16-user-centric-credential-model-design.md` (sub-project C, never specced until now) and the 2026-09-16 multi-credential decisions (memory `project_multi_credential_types_plan`).

## Goal

A user can hold a password as well as, or instead of, a PIN. Lock Code Manager writes it to every lock in the entry that takes passwords and keeps it in sync there, the way it does PINs today.

## Scope

In:

- Password as a second managed credential type, end to end: sync core, storage, Z-Wave and Virtual providers, entities, config, services, websocket, slot card, add-user card and lock card.
- Making the core type-generic, so that RFID and NFC can later be added as data, not as structure.

Out:

- RFID, NFC and biometrics.
- A pattern on the PIN entity (see "Text entities").
- Showing or editing unmanaged passwords on the lock card.
- User Code CC locks whose keypad accepts non-digit characters. The driver uses the Password type for these (`node-zwave-js AccessControl.ts:1598`), and they may be invisible to Lock Code Manager today. Follow-up issue.

## Decisions

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | Passwords are printable ASCII, 0x20–0x7E, spaces included. The Z-Wave spec requires passwords to travel as UTF-16 big endian (CC:0083.01.0A.11.021) and counts Credential Length in bytes (.0A.11.014/.015). 2026A's worked example gives a 17-character password a length of 34. Every printable ASCII character is exactly 2 bytes, so the per-lock length check compares `2 × len(password)` against the lock's limits. |
| 2 | The sync core is keyed by `CredentialAddress(slot, type)`. There is still one worker per lock. |
| 3 | Release stays per slot: one release removes every type Lock Code Manager wrote for the slot. |
| 4 | A slot needs at least one credential of any type. Clearing a credential disables the slot only when no other credential remains. A stored value counts even if no current lock takes its type. |
| 5 | On Z-Wave, the password index is allocated by the provider: it finds the tagged user's password wherever it is, or else takes the lowest password index no user holds. PIN keeps following the slot. |
| 6 | Credential text entities set no `pattern`, `native_min` or `native_max`. One validator and the coordinator's per-lock length check are the only gates, and their errors never contain the value. |
| 7 | Passwords are not whitespace-stripped. PINs keep `vol.Strip`. |
| 8 | Slot card: tabs per type over one value field, each tab's dot showing that type's sync state. Tabs appear only when the entry offers more than one type. |
| 9 | Lock card: tabs per type. The PIN tab is today's card. The Password tab lists managed users' passwords on that lock. |
| 10 | Carried from 2026-09-16: an entry's available types are the union across its locks. A type no longer offered keeps its stored value, and its entity is removed. Per-type in-sync sensors are disabled by default. Duplicates are refused within a type and allowed across types. The generator covers passwords. |

## Sync core

`CredentialAddress(user_ref, credential_type)` already exists (`model/credentials.py`). It becomes the key everywhere in `sync/`:

- `LockWorker.slots: dict[CredentialAddress, Slot]`. `want`, `forget`, `resume`, `status`, `syncing` and `push` take an address.
- `LockPort.read(addresses) -> Mapping[CredentialAddress, Reading]` and `LockPort.write(address, value) -> bool | None`.
- `sync/slot.py` stays a single-value state machine. `Holds.pin` becomes `Holds.value`, `Want` stays `str | None`, and `Holds.__repr__` keeps masking.
- `sync/registry.py` and `ha/adapter.py` re-key to match. The adapter turns an address into the provider call for that type.
- Release is per slot. When a slot leaves the entry, the worker sends one release for the slot. The provider removes every credential Lock Code Manager wrote to that slot's user, then the user only if it holds nothing else.

**Managed addresses are per lock:** `{CredentialAddress(slot, t) for t in lock.capabilities.credential_types ∩ MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES}`. This covers every type the lock takes, not only the types the user has a value for. A user with no password still gets a password address on a password lock, with want `None`, so a password cleared or never set is kept cleared, the same way an empty PIN is kept cleared today. A lock that doesn't take password never gets a password address, so the aggregate `in_sync` on that lock ignores the type. This fixes the global `managed_addresses()` gap found in the #1572 review. Recompute when a lock is added or removed and when capabilities refresh.

`MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES` becomes `{PIN, PASSWORD}`.

## Storage

`ha/lock_store.py`, `STORE_VERSION` 1 → 2.

- v1 slot record: `{"wrote": <fingerprint|cleared>, …release fields}`.
- v2 slot record: `{"wrote": {"pin": <fingerprint|cleared>, "password": REDACTED, …release fields}`.
- Migration: move v1 `wrote` under `"pin"`. Release fields stay at slot level.
- The fingerprint covers the type: `fingerprint(type, value, salt)`. Credential values are never persisted.

The Store migration is the only one-way step. Downgrading leaves a v2 Store the old version can't read, and HA's Store versioning is there to refuse that.

## Configuration and the credential-required rule

- The user subentry gets an optional `password` (absent means none), and setup YAML gets `password:` per user. No config-entry migration is needed.
- The rule changes in four places:
  - `ha/slot_coordinator.py:294`: clearing any credential disables an enabled slot only if no other credential remains.
  - `ha/slot_coordinator.py:355`: enabling is refused only when the user has no credential of any type. `PinRequiredError` becomes `CredentialRequiredError`.
  - `config_flow.py:84-93, 422`: `_slot_enabled_without_pin` becomes `_slot_enabled_without_credential`, which checks every managed type's field.
  - Repair `pin_required` becomes `credential_required`. Update `switch.py:62`, `ha/services.py:451`, `repairs.py:179` and `__init__.py:1220`. At startup, delete any leftover `pin_required_*` issue.

**Z-Wave (`providers/zwave_js.py`)**

| Schlage | One access code, `^\d{4,8}$` | No | pyschlage `code.py:164-188`; HA `schlage/__init__.py:37` |
| Akuvox | `private_pin` (4–8 digits), `card_code` | No | pylocal-akuvox `users.py:19-47`; local_akuvox `validation.py:53-65` |

The Silicon Labs reference firmware validates only PIN data (`cc_user_credential_validation.c:87-110`), so it would store UTF-8 bytes without rejecting them. PR 4 waits for the driver fix (zwave-js/zwave-js#9396).

So a minimum HA version can't guarantee a driver. PR 4 adds a setup-time check: compare `client.version.driver_version` against the first release containing #9396. If the driver is older, refuse to set up the lock with an error naming the required version. This applies to every Z-Wave lock, not only ones with passwords. It's a breaking change for users on older drivers, so the PR gets a Breaking Change section. The same check replaces the "guaranteed by the integration's minimum Home Assistant version" claim in `zwave_js.py:200-203` about 15.24.3.

## Entities and validation

It's called from the coordinator, the config flow, `add_user`, `set_credential` and the setup YAML schema. Error text names the rule and never the value. For example: "Password may only contain letters, digits, symbols and spaces".

**Length:** `_validate_credential_length(value, type)` (`slot_coordinator.py:303`) is called for password against password-capable locks only. Its message already names each lock and its range.

**Labels:** add `"password": "Password"` to `CREDENTIAL_LABELS` (`const.py:210`) and `ts/const.ts`, which a contract test checks. That gives:

**Masking:** `mask_pin` becomes `mask_credential`, used in every log line that carries a value.

**Generator:** `generate_pin` becomes `generate_credential(type, length)`. For password it uses the printable ASCII set, at a length inside every password-capable lock's range in the entry.

## Services and websocket

"""
One slot on one lock: what is wanted, what was written, what the lock said.

Pure: no Home Assistant, no asyncio; the worker passes the time in. The
rules are the credential-model decisions as the first-principles design
states them (docs: 2026-10-13-core-first-principles.md).
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum, StrEnum
import hashlib
from typing import override

# What the lock said about a slot.


class Seen(Enum):
    """What the lock said about a slot, apart from which PIN it holds."""

    EMPTY = "empty"
    # Holds a code it will not show.
    MASKED = "masked"
    # Holds a code that is not in force.
    DISABLED = "disabled"
    # Answered without saying anything about the slot.
    SILENT = "silent"


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Holds:
    """The slot holds this PIN, and the lock said so."""

    pin: str = field(repr=False)

    @override
    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Keep the PIN out of logs (#917)."""
        return "Holds(****)"


Reading = Seen | Holds

# A wanted PIN, or None for an empty slot.
Want = str | None


class Repair(StrEnum):
    """Why a slot is held, and what the user is told."""

    # The lock refused the PIN; the slot is turned off.
    SLOT_DISABLED = "slot_disabled"
    # The PIN would not go on; nothing is written until the target changes.
    CANT_SET = "cant_set"
    # A clear would not take: the code may still open the door.
    CODE_MAY_REMAIN = "code_may_remain"


class Status(StrEnum):
    """A slot's sync status, as the integration shows it."""

    UNKNOWN = "unknown"
    IN_SYNC = "in_sync"
    OUT_OF_SYNC = "out_of_sync"
    SUSPENDED = "suspended"


CLEARED = "cleared"
WINDOW = 300.0
LIMIT = 3
RELEASE_LIMIT = 2


def fingerprint(pin: str, salt: bytes) -> str:
    """Return a salted fingerprint of ``pin``: kept and persisted instead of it."""
    return hashlib.blake2b(pin.encode(), key=salt, digest_size=16).hexdigest()


@dataclass
class Slot:
    """
    One slot on one lock.

    ``wrote`` is what was last written and returned without error: a PIN's
    fingerprint, or ``CLEARED``. ``release`` marks a slot no entry manages any
    more, being cleared on its way out.

    Two counts hold a slot. ``tries`` counts syncs that did not end in sync
    while the lock was there, since the target last changed or a fresh read
    last agreed; they never expire, so no pattern of retries can go on for
    ever. ``fights`` counts
    times the lock went from agreeing to disagreeing -- a keypad taking the
    code back (#776) -- and ages out of ``WINDOW``.

    A hold is lifted by a change of target or the user acknowledging its
    repair. One from tries running out also lifts itself when a fresh read
    shows the lock already agrees: whatever kept the write from landing, the
    slot is as wanted now. One from fights or a refusal never does: a keypad
    fighting the code back agrees between fights, and the lock said no.
    """

    want: Want
    wrote: str | None = None
    seen: Reading | None = None
    tries: int = 0
    fights: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)
    hold: Repair | None = None
    # The hold came from tries running out: a fresh agreeing read lifts it.
    liftable: bool = False
    release: bool = False
    # What the lock or its driver said when it refused the slot, if anything.
    why: str = ""
    # The cause the provider named for the last failed write, if it named one.
    cause: str = ""
    # A release has been sent and answered: it reaches the lock once.
    released: bool = False
    # Bumped each time the counts start over: a sync begun before is not
    # charged to what came after.
    epoch: int = 0
    # After a failed try, no write before this time (the worker's clock): a
    # pause that only a new target or a resume ends, never a report.
    not_before: float | None = None

    def aim(self, want: Want, *, release: bool = False) -> None:
        """Set what is wanted; a change of target starts the counts over."""
        if want != self.want or release != self.release:
            self.resume()
        if release and not self.release:
            self.released = False
        self.want = want
        self.release = release

    def agrees(self, salt: bytes) -> bool:
        """Return whether what the lock said agrees with what is wanted."""
        seen = self.seen
        if self.want is None:
            if self.release and not self.released:
                # A release reaches the lock once, whatever it says: a lock
                # with users tears down the one this slot anchored, even
                # with no code on it.
                return False
            if seen is Seen.EMPTY:
                return True
            # A lock that will not show its codes, or says nothing, may go on
            # calling the slot occupied after a clear (#1437): trust the clear.
            return seen in (Seen.MASKED, Seen.SILENT) and self.wrote == CLEARED
        written = self.wrote == fingerprint(self.want, salt)
        if isinstance(seen, Holds):
            return seen.pin == self.want
        # A lock that will not show the code, or says nothing: trust the write.
        # A limit, not a bug: a write the lock dropped on a slot it never reads
        # back looks the same from here as one it took. The views label such a
        # slot withheld or unanswered, so the user sees it is trusted, not read.
        return seen in (Seen.MASKED, Seen.SILENT) and written

    def doubt(self, salt: bytes) -> None:
        """
        Forget what the lock said if it agrees with what is wanted.

        For a reading that may be older than a write to another target: if
        that write landed, an agreeing reading could pass the slot as in
        sync, so the slot is read first. One that disagrees only leads to a
        write, so it stands: the slot shows out of sync, pending, not
        unknown. So does silence: it agrees only through ``wrote``, which a
        write to another target clears when it is sent, and reading a silent
        slot again only hears silence.
        """
        if self.seen is not Seen.SILENT and self.agrees(salt):
            self.seen = None

    def status(self, salt: bytes) -> Status:
        """Return the slot's sync status."""
        if self.hold is not None:
            return Status.SUSPENDED
        if self.seen is None:
            return Status.UNKNOWN
        return Status.IN_SYNC if self.agrees(salt) else Status.OUT_OF_SYNC

    def observe(
        self, reading: Reading, salt: bytes, now: float, *, fresh: bool = True
    ) -> None:
        """
        Take what the lock said about the slot.

        A fresh read that agrees starts the tries over, and lifts a hold
        from tries running out; a push may come from a cache, so it never
        does. Going from agreeing to disagreeing is a fight, and the write
        behind the agreement is no longer trusted.
        """
        agreed = self.seen is not None and self.agrees(salt)
        self.seen = reading
        if self.agrees(salt):
            if fresh and self.liftable:
                self.resume()
            elif fresh:
                self.tries = 0
        elif agreed:
            self.wrote = None
            self.fought(now)

    def wrote_want(self, salt: bytes) -> None:
        """Record that a write of what is wanted returned without error."""
        self.wrote = self._target(salt)

    def _target(self, salt: bytes) -> str:
        """Return what ``wrote`` holds once what is wanted has been written."""
        return CLEARED if self.want is None else fingerprint(self.want, salt)

    def tried(self) -> None:
        """Count a sync that did not end in sync, with the lock there."""
        self.tries += 1
        if self.tries >= self._limit():
            self.hold, self.liftable = self._give_up(), True

    def fought(self, now: float) -> None:
        """
        Count the lock going from agreeing to disagreeing.

        Agreement never clears these, so a keypad fighting a code back trips
        (#776); they age out of ``WINDOW``.
        """
        self.fights = [t for t in self.fights if t > now - WINDOW]
        self.fights.append(now)
        if len(self.fights) >= self._limit():
            self.hold, self.liftable = self._give_up(), False

    def _limit(self) -> int:
        return RELEASE_LIMIT if self.release else LIMIT

    def refused(self, *, value: bool, why: str = "") -> None:
        """Hold the slot at once: the lock refused the value, or the slot."""
        self.why, self.cause, self.liftable = why, "", False
        if value and self.want is not None:
            self.hold = Repair.SLOT_DISABLED
        else:
            self.hold = self._give_up()

    def resume(self) -> None:
        """Lift any hold and start the counts over."""
        self.epoch += 1
        self.tries = 0
        self.fights.clear()
        self.hold = None
        self.liftable = False
        self.not_before = None
        self.why = self.cause = ""

    def _give_up(self) -> Repair:
        return Repair.CODE_MAY_REMAIN if self.want is None else Repair.CANT_SET
"""
One worker per lock, shared by every entry that manages it.

Entries hold a lock and claim its slots. A slot has one owner at most; only
its owner sets what it holds. The lock's worker runs while an entry holds
the lock or a slot given up is still being cleared, and is stopped when
neither is true. Pure asyncio: the integration passes in how a worker is
built, how its lock is prepared before the worker first reads it (the
provider's setup), and how it is cleaned up after the worker stops.
"""

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Collection, Mapping
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
import itertools
import logging
from typing import Any

from .slot import Reading, Want
from .worker import LockPort, LockWorker

_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)

type Hook[P: LockPort] = Callable[[str, LockWorker[P]], Awaitable[None]]


async def _nothing(lock: str, worker: LockWorker[Any]) -> None:
    """Prepare or clean up nothing."""


class SlotTaken(Exception):
    """Another entry owns the slot."""

    def __init__(self, slot: int, owner: str) -> None:
        """Name the slot and its owner."""
        super().__init__(f"slot {slot} is owned by {owner}")
        self.slot = slot
        self.owner = owner


@dataclass
class _Lock[P: LockPort]:
    worker: LockWorker[P]
    holders: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    # Slot -> the entry that owns it. A slot given up has no owner.
    owners: dict[int, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # Preparing the lock, once an entry holds it: never for a one-off read.
    prepared: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None


class LockRegistry[P: LockPort]:
    """Lock id -> its one worker; which entries hold it and own which slots."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        make_worker: Callable[[str], LockWorker[P]],
        grace: float = 30.0,
        *,
        prepare: Hook[P] = _nothing,
        cleanup: Hook[P] = _nothing,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Build workers with ``make_worker``; give each ``grace`` to stop.

        ``prepare`` runs once an entry holds the lock, before a new worker's
        first read; ``cleanup`` runs after every worker stops, once
        ``prepare`` is done if it ran -- a one-off read's worker included.
        """
        self._make = make_worker
        self._grace = grace
        self._prepare = prepare
        self._cleanup = cleanup
        self._locks: dict[str, _Lock[P]] = {}
        self._stops: dict[str, asyncio.Task[None]] = {}
        self._once = itertools.count()
        self._closed = False

    async def hold(
        self, lock: str, owner: str, wants: Mapping[int, Want] | None = None
    ) -> LockWorker[P]:
        """
        Hold ``lock`` for ``owner``, claiming ``wants``' slots; return its worker.

        A new worker is prepared, then starts with every slot wanted so far,
        so its first read takes them all at once. A worker still stopping is
        waited for: one lock never has two. Once the registry has stopped,
        nothing is held.
        """
        return await self._hold(lock, owner, wants or {}, prepare=True)

    async def _hold(
        self, lock: str, owner: str, wants: Mapping[int, Want], *, prepare: bool
    ) -> LockWorker[P]:
        while (stopping := self._stops.get(lock)) is not None:
            # Not shield: a stop cancelled with stop()'s caller is still done.
            await asyncio.wait({stopping})
        if self._closed:
            raise RuntimeError("the lock registry has stopped")
        if new := (entry := self._locks.get(lock)) is None:
            worker = self._make(lock)
            entry = self._locks[lock] = _Lock(worker)
            inner = worker.on_change

            def _on_change() -> None:
                try:
                    inner()
                finally:
                    # The worker logs what ``inner`` raises; stopping goes on.
                    self._maybe_stop(lock)

            worker.on_change = _on_change
        else:
            _check_free(entry, owner, wants)
        entry.holders.add(owner)
        for slot, pin in wants.items():
            entry.owners[slot] = owner
            entry.worker.want(slot, pin)
        joined = None
        if prepare and entry.prepared is None:
            entry.prepared = asyncio.create_task(self._prepared(lock, entry.worker))
            if not new:
                # A one-off read's worker, already started: what it asked the

def _ms(start: float) -> float:

        ``cause`` is set only when the provider named, for the user, why it
        failed.

        super().__init__(message or kind.value)
        self.kind = kind
        self.sent = sent
        self.message = message
        self.cause = cause


class LockPort(Protocol):

    async def read(self, slots: Collection[int]) -> Mapping[int, Reading]:

    async def write(self, slot: int, pin: str | None) -> bool | None:

    result: Any = None,
    error: BaseException | None = None,
) -> None:

        self._task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None

        self._started = False
        self._stopping = False

        self._queued: set[int] = set()
        # The slot whose sync is running now.

        self._seq = 0
        self._sent = 0
        self._written: dict[int, int] = {}
        self._last_exchange: float | None = None

        self._answers = 0
        # The provider raised something that is not a LockError.

        # The lock took a write, and the read-back went unanswered.
        self._lost = False
        # Slots charged a try since the lock last answered, by Slot and epoch:

        # said before is no guide to a new target.

        answer, as always, decides whether the lock is there.

            return

    @property

    @property

    @property
    def offline(self) -> bool:

        A lock that answers for some slots and not others never gets here:
        a slot whose own exchanges go unanswered while another slot answers

        offline (#1257); one that answered an earlier run and is dead at
        this one's start is.

    def request_sync(

    ) -> None:

        Before ``start`` nothing is queued: the first read comes first.
        ``why`` is only for the logs.

        if not self._started:
            return
        for slot in tuple(self.slots if slots is None else slots):
            if slot not in self._queued:
                self._queued.add(slot)

    def push(self, slot: int, reading: Reading) -> None:

        A report taken in before the slot's last write finished is dropped
        when its turn comes: the write's read-back is newer.
        """

            "%s slot %s: push received, %s ms since last write sent",
            self.name,
            slot,

    async def read(
        self, slots: Collection[int] | None = None, *, probe: bool = False
    ) -> dict[int, Reading]:

        A held slot is left out of the read -- a lock that fails a read over
        one slot it ignores would otherwise fail every poll of the rest --
        and one whose hold an agreeing read lifts (``Slot.liftable``) is read
        after it, on its own (``_read_held``). ``probe`` when someone says
        the lock may be back (the hard refresh service): the read goes even
        while backing off, and an answer brings the lock back.

            raise LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message="stopped")

            held = tuple(n for n, slot in self.slots.items() if slot.liftable)

            _Job("probe" if probe else "read", slots=wanted, held=held, done=done),
            "caller",

    async def turn[T](self, call: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> T:

        Run ``call`` against the lock in its turn, as one exchange; return its result.

        For a question about the lock asked through a provider of its own (the
        migration's unmanaged-code sweep): nothing else talks to the lock
        meanwhile, and its answer counts like any other.
        """
        if self._stopping:
            raise LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message="stopped")
        done: asyncio.Future[T] = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
        self._put(_Job("turn", call=call, done=done), "caller")
        return await done

        """Wait until every job queued so far, and any it queued, is done."""
        await self._queue.join()

    def start(self) -> None:

        self.request_sync(why="start")

    async def stop(self, grace: float = 30.0) -> None:
        """
        Stop for good.

        No new jobs are taken, waiting ones are answered at once, and the job
        running now gets ``grace`` to finish before it is cancelled.
        """
        if self._stopping:
            await self._stopped.wait()
            return

            self._drain()

                        await asyncio.shield(self._task)

                    await asyncio.wait({self._task}, timeout=grace)

            # queued (a cancelled task never reaches the end-of-queue marker),

            self._drain()

    def _drain(self) -> None:

        while not self._queue.empty():
            job = self._queue.get_nowait()
            if job is not None:
                _resolve(
                    job.done,
                    error=LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message="stopped"),

            self._queue.task_done()

    def _put(self, job: _Job, why: str | None) -> None:
        """Queue ``job``; log why, unless ``why`` is None (logged already)."""
        if not self._stopping:
            if why is not None:
                _LOGGER.debug(
                    "%s slot %s: queued %s (%s)",
                    self.name,
                    _where(job.slot, job.slots),
                    job.kind,
                    why,
                )
            self._queue.put_nowait(job)
            self._woken.set()

    async def _run(self) -> None:

            if self._stopping and self._queue.empty():
                return  # it ate stop's cancel; nothing is left to do
            if (job := await self._take()) is None:
                break
            before = self._statuses()
            try:
                await self._do(job)
            except LockError as err:
                _resolve(job.done, error=err)
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                # Cut off by stop: its caller still gets an answer.
                _resolve(
                    job.done,
                    error=LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message="stopped"),

                _LOGGER.exception("Lock job %s failed", job.kind)
                _resolve(job.done, error=err)
            finally:
                self._queue.task_done()
            self._log_transitions(before, job.kind)
            try:
                self.on_change()
            except Exception:  # the integration's trouble must not stop the lock
                _LOGGER.exception("Lock change callback failed")

    async def _take(self) -> _Job | None:
        """
        Take the next job, queueing slots and the probe as they fall due.

        The worker owns every timer: with nothing queued, the loop waits for
        the first slot's pause or the next probe to end, or for a job.
        """
        while self._queue.empty() and (deadline := self._deadline()) is not None:
            if (wait := deadline - self.clock()) > 0:
                self._woken.clear()
                timer = asyncio.ensure_future(self.sleep(wait))
                woken = asyncio.ensure_future(self._woken.wait())

                    await asyncio.wait(
                        (timer, woken), return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED
                    )

                    timer.cancel()
                    woken.cancel()

        return await self._queue.get()

    def _deadline(self) -> float | None:
        """Return when the first slot's pause or the next probe ends, if any."""
        times = [s.not_before for s in self.slots.values() if s.not_before is not None]
        if self._probe_at is not None and self.slots:
            times.append(self._probe_at)

    def _fire(self) -> None:

                self.request_sync((number,), why="retry")
        if self._probe_at is not None and self._probe_at <= self.clock():
            self._probe()

    def _paused(self, slot: Slot) -> bool:
        """Return whether ``slot`` is waiting out a pause; forget one that is over."""
        if slot.not_before is not None and slot.not_before <= self.clock():
            slot.not_before = None
        return slot.not_before is not None

    def _statuses(self) -> dict[int, Status] | None:
        """Return each slot's status, for logging its changes; None if not logged."""
        if not _LOGGER.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG):
            return None
        return {number: slot.status(self.salt) for number, slot in self.slots.items()}

    def _log_transitions(self, before: dict[int, Status] | None, kind: str) -> None:
        """Log each slot whose status a job changed."""
        if before is None:
            return
        for number, slot in self.slots.items():
            if (was := before.get(number)) is not (now := slot.status(self.salt)):

                    "%s slot %s: status %s -> %s (after %s)",
                    self.name,
                    number,
                    was,
                    now,
                    kind,

            _resolve(job.done, error=LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False))

            _resolve(job.done, await self._exchange(job.call, op="turn"))

    async def _read_held(self, number: int) -> dict[int, Reading]:

        Read a slot held after its tries on its own: an agreeing reading lifts it.

        failure is nobody's: a slot the lock ignores, held for that, never
        backs the lock off or fails the read of the rest.

            return await self._read((number,), op="held read", count=False)
        except LockError:

430	
431	    async def _run(self) -> None:
432	        while True:
433	            if self._stopping and self._queue.empty():
434	                return  # it ate stop's cancel; nothing is left to do
435	            if (job := await self._take()) is None:
436	                break
437	            before = self._statuses()
438	            try:
439	                await self._do(job)
440	            except LockError as err:
441	                _resolve(job.done, error=err)
442	            except asyncio.CancelledError:
443	                # Cut off by stop: its caller still gets an answer.
444	                _resolve(
445	                    job.done,
446	                    error=LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message="stopped"),
447	                )
448	                raise
449	            except Exception as err:  # one bad job must not stop the lock
450	                _LOGGER.exception("Lock job %s failed", job.kind)
451	                _resolve(job.done, error=err)
452	            finally:
453	                self._queue.task_done()
454	            self._log_transitions(before, job.kind)
455	            try:
456	                self.on_change()
457	            except Exception:  # the integration's trouble must not stop the lock
458	                _LOGGER.exception("Lock change callback failed")
459	        self._queue.task_done()
460	
461	    async def _take(self) -> _Job | None:
462	        """
463	        Take the next job, queueing slots and the probe as they fall due.
464	
465	        The worker owns every timer: with nothing queued, the loop waits for
466	        the first slot's pause or the next probe to end, or for a job.
467	        """
468	        while self._queue.empty() and (deadline := self._deadline()) is not None:
469	            if (wait := deadline - self.clock()) > 0:
470	                self._woken.clear()
471	                timer = asyncio.ensure_future(self.sleep(wait))
472	                woken = asyncio.ensure_future(self._woken.wait())
473	                try:
474	                    await asyncio.wait(
475	                        (timer, woken), return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED
476	                    )
477	                finally:
478	                    timer.cancel()
479	                    woken.cancel()
480	            self._fire()
481	        return await self._queue.get()
482	
483	    def _deadline(self) -> float | None:
484	        """Return when the first slot's pause or the next probe ends, if any."""
485	        times = [s.not_before for s in self.slots.values() if s.not_before is not None]
486	        if self._probe_at is not None and self.slots:
487	            times.append(self._probe_at)
488	        return min(times, default=None)
489	
490	    def _fire(self) -> None:
491	        """Queue each slot whose pause is over, and the probe if it is due."""
492	        for number, slot in tuple(self.slots.items()):
493	            if slot.not_before is not None and not self._paused(slot):
494	                self.request_sync((number,), why="retry")
495	        if self._probe_at is not None and self._probe_at <= self.clock():
496	            self._probe()
497	
498	    def _paused(self, slot: Slot) -> bool:
499	        """Return whether ``slot`` is waiting out a pause; forget one that is over."""
500	        if slot.not_before is not None and slot.not_before <= self.clock():
501	            slot.not_before = None
502	        return slot.not_before is not None
503	
504	    def _statuses(self) -> dict[int, Status] | None:
505	        """Return each slot's status, for logging its changes; None if not logged."""
506	        if not _LOGGER.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG):
507	            return None
508	        return {number: slot.status(self.salt) for number, slot in self.slots.items()}
509	
510	    def _log_transitions(self, before: dict[int, Status] | None, kind: str) -> None:
511	        """Log each slot whose status a job changed."""
512	        if before is None:
513	            return
514	        for number, slot in self.slots.items():
515	            if (was := before.get(number)) is not (now := slot.status(self.salt)):
516	                _LOGGER.debug(
517	                    "%s slot %s: status %s -> %s (after %s)",
518	                    self.name,
519	                    number,
520	                    was,
521	                    now,
522	                    kind,
523	                )

525	    async def _do(self, job: _Job) -> None:
526	        if job.kind == "push":
527	            self._take_push(job)
528	            return
529	        if job.kind == "slot":
530	            assert job.slot is not None
531	            self._queued.discard(job.slot)
532	        if self._down_until is not None and job.kind != "probe":
533	            # Backing off: callers hear at once that the lock is not
534	            # answering; slot syncs are queued again once it answers.
535	            _resolve(job.done, error=LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False))
536	            return
537	        if job.kind == "slot":
538	            assert job.slot is not None
539	            self._syncing = job.slot
540	            try:
541	                await self._sync(job.slot)
542	            finally:
543	                self._syncing = None
544	            self._again(job.slot)
545	            return
546	        if job.kind == "turn":
547	            assert job.call is not None
548	            _resolve(job.done, await self._exchange(job.call, op="turn"))
549	            return
550	        # A probe left unanswered schedules the next one through _no_answer.
551	        readings = await self._read(job.slots, op=job.kind)
552	        for number in job.held:
553	            readings.update(await self._read_held(number))
554	        _resolve(job.done, readings)
555	
556	    async def _read_held(self, number: int) -> dict[int, Reading]:
557	        """
558	        Read a slot held after its tries on its own: an agreeing reading lifts it.
559	
560	        Nothing is written or charged for it whatever it says, and its
561	        failure is nobody's: a slot the lock ignores, held for that, never
562	        backs the lock off or fails the read of the rest.
563	        """
564	        try:
565	            return await self._read((number,), op="held read", count=False)
566	        except LockError:
567	            return {}
568	
569	    def _take_push(self, job: _Job) -> None:
570	        assert job.slot is not None and job.reading is not None
571	        slot = self.slots.get(job.slot)
572	        if slot is None or self._written.get(job.slot, 0) > job.seq:
573	            _LOGGER.debug(
574	                "%s slot %s: push dropped (untracked, or older than the last write)",
575	                self.name,
576	                job.slot,
577	            )
578	            return
579	        if self._unsure_of(job.slot, slot):
580	            # A report may be a cache older than that write: it is no fight,
581	            # and no reason to stop trusting what was written.
582	            slot.seen = job.reading
583	            slot.doubt(self.salt)
584	        else:
585	            slot.observe(job.reading, self.salt, self.clock(), fresh=False)
586	        self.request_sync((job.slot,), why="push")
587	
588	    def _unsure_of(self, number: int, slot: Slot) -> bool:
589	        """Return whether a write for another target may have landed since a reading."""
590	        unsure = self._unsure.get(number)
591	        return unsure is not None and (unsure[0] is not slot or unsure[1] != slot.epoch)
592	
593	    async def _sync(self, number: int) -> None:
594	        """
595	        Bring one slot in line: read it if never read, write it if it differs.
596	
597	        A sync that ends out of sync costs the slot one try, charged once the
598	        lock has shown it is there: at once if anything in the sync was
599	        answered, else when the lock next answers. Between two answers a slot
600	        is charged once at most, so an outage costs it one try at most. A
601	        provider bug is the slot's: charged at once, every time. Nothing is
602	        awaited between looking and charging, and a sync begun before the
603	        counts started over is not charged.
604	
605	        So every sync that does not end in sync is charged, or owed while
606	        nothing answers -- and only an answer resets the lock's no-answers:
607	        each slot ends in sync, held, or with the lock offline.
608	        """
609	        if (slot := self.slots.get(number)) is None:
610	            return
611	        epoch, answers, self._bug = slot.epoch, self._answers, False
612	        # Waiting out a pause: a read still goes, but nothing is written or
613	        # charged before the pause ends -- whatever queued this sync.
614	        paused = self._paused(slot)
615	        try:
616	            if slot.status(self.salt) is Status.UNKNOWN:
617	                await self._read((number,), follow=False, op="first read")
618	            if slot.status(self.salt) is Status.OUT_OF_SYNC and not paused:
619	                await self._write(number, slot)
620	        except LockError as err:
621	            _LOGGER.debug("Sync of slot %s failed: %s", number, err)
622	            if err.kind is ErrorKind.SLOT_REFUSED and slot.epoch == epoch:
623	                # A read refused for the slot (past the lock's capacity).
624	                slot.refused(value=False, why=err.message)
625	        if slot.epoch == epoch and not paused and self._failed(slot):
626	            if self._bug:
627	                slot.tried()
628	            elif self._answers > answers and not self._lost:
629	                self._charge(number, slot)
630	            elif not self._was_charged(number, slot):
631	                self._owed[number] = (slot, epoch)
632	        # A read-back lost in this sync is settled: owed, or nothing to owe.
633	        self._lost = False
634	        if (
635	            slot.release
636	            and slot.status(self.salt) is Status.IN_SYNC
637	            and self.slots.get(number) is slot
638	        ):
639	            del self.slots[number]
640	
641	    def _failed(self, slot: Slot) -> bool:
642	        return slot.status(self.salt) in (Status.UNKNOWN, Status.OUT_OF_SYNC)
643	
644	    def _charge(self, number: int, slot: Slot) -> None:
645	        """Charge ``slot`` one try, unless charged since the lock last answered."""
646	        if not self._was_charged(number, slot):
647	            self._charged[number] = (slot, slot.epoch)
648	            slot.tried()
649	
650	    def _was_charged(self, number: int, slot: Slot) -> bool:
651	        """Return whether this target was charged since the lock last answered."""
652	        charged = self._charged.get(number)
653	        return charged is not None and charged[0] is slot and charged[1] == slot.epoch
654	
655	    async def _write(self, number: int, slot: Slot) -> None:
656	        """
657	        Write what is wanted, then read it back.
658	
659	        What was sent is what is recorded; if the slot changed hands or wants
660	        another PIN by the time the write is back, nothing is recorded or read
661	        back; the write may have landed, so ``want`` doubted what the lock
662	        last said (``Slot.doubt``). A refusal holds at once.
663	        Anything else, even a write that never left, is read back -- unless
664	        the lock has just gone into backoff -- and a cause the provider named
665	        is kept, so a slot held after its tries says it.
666	
667	        A read-back left unanswered after a write the lock took is owed, not
668	        charged: the slot is read afresh next, and only that answer says
669	        whether the write failed (#1397). Silence is never an answer: it
670	        still counts toward the lock backing off.
671	        """
672	        pin = slot.want
673	        slot.wrote = None
674	        took = False
675	
676	        def current() -> bool:
677	            # Still the slot in place, still wanting what was sent.
678	            return self.slots.get(number) is slot and slot.want == pin
679	
680	        op = "clear" if pin is None else "set"
681	        # Forgotten or retargeted while waiting its turn: send nothing.
682	        await self._pace(op, number)
683	        if not current():
684	            return
685	        self._unsure[number] = (slot, slot.epoch)
686	        try:
687	            self.on_send()
688	        except Exception:  # the integration's trouble must not stop the lock
689	            _LOGGER.exception("Lock send callback failed")
690	        try:
691	            # Reports taken in before the write is sent are older than it.
692	            changed = await self._exchange(
693	                lambda: self.port.write(number, pin), mark=number, op=op
694	            )
695	        except LockError as err:
696	            if not current():
697	                return
698	            # If it is held after its tries, a cause the provider named says why.
699	            slot.cause = err.cause
700	            if err.kind is ErrorKind.ALREADY_SO:
701	                slot.wrote_want(self.salt)
702	                slot.released = slot.release
703	                took = True
704	            elif err.kind is ErrorKind.VALUE_REFUSED:
705	                slot.refused(value=True, why=err.message)
706	                if pin is not None:
707	                    self.on_disable(number)
708	                return
709	            elif err.kind is ErrorKind.SLOT_REFUSED:
710	                slot.refused(value=False, why=err.message)
711	                return
712	        else:
713	            if not current():
714	                return
715	            slot.cause = ""
716	            slot.released = slot.release
717	            if changed is not False:
718	                slot.wrote_want(self.salt)
719	            took = True
720	        if self._down_until is None:
721	            missed = self._no_answers
722	            try:
723	                await self._read((number,), follow=False, op="read-back")
724	            except LockError:
725	                if took and self._no_answers > missed:
726	                    slot.seen = None
727	                    self._lost = True
728	                raise
729	
730	    def _next(self) -> int:
731	        """Return the next point in the order reports and exchanges happen."""
732	        self._seq += 1
733	        return self._seq
734	
735	    async def _read(
736	        self,
737	        numbers: Collection[int],
738	        *,
739	        follow: bool = True,
740	        op: str = "read",
741	        count: bool = True,
742	    ) -> dict[int, Reading]:
743	        """
744	        Read ``numbers``; unless ``follow`` is off, queue any slot that needs work.
745	
746	        A slot whose hold the reading lifted is synced again: nothing to
747	        write, but a release in sync is done. ``count`` off: no answer is not
748	        counted against the lock.
749	
750	        A reading is newer than every report on its slot taken in before the
751	        read was sent; one taken in while it was out may be newer, and is
752	        kept. A slot the read left out says nothing, and drops no report.
753	        """
754	        if not numbers:
755	            # Reading nothing asks the lock nothing: no answer, no no-answer.
756	            return {}
757	
758	        async def _readings() -> dict[int, Reading]:
759	            # Inside the exchange: a provider returning garbage is its bug.
760	            return dict(await self.port.read(numbers))
761	
762	        readings = await self._exchange(
763	            _readings, pay=False, op=op, slots=tuple(numbers), count=count
764	        )
765	        due = self._due()
766	        for number in numbers:
767	            if number in readings:
768	                self._written[number] = self._sent
769	                self._unsure.pop(number, None)
770	            reading = readings.setdefault(number, Seen.SILENT)
771	            if (slot := self.slots.get(number)) is not None:
772	                held = slot.hold is not None
773	                slot.observe(reading, self.salt, self.clock())
774	                if held and slot.hold is None:
775	                    self.request_sync((number,), why="hold lifted")
776	                elif follow:
777	                    self._again(number)
778	        self._pay(due)
779	        return readings
780	
781	    def _again(self, number: int) -> None:
782	        """
783	        Queue another sync of ``number`` if it still needs one.
784	
785	        Every sync that does not end in sync is charged to the slot, or owed
786	        until the lock next answers -- and with no answer, the lock backs off
787	        on its way to the offline repair. So this ends in sync, held, or with
788	        the lock offline -- never in a loop. (A job queued while backing off
789	        fails at once, and an answer queues every slot again.)
790	        """
791	        slot = self.slots.get(number)
792	        # Already waiting out a pause: the loop queues it when the pause ends.
793	        if slot is None or not self._failed(slot) or slot.not_before is not None:
794	            return
795	        delay = RETRY_AFTER[min(slot.tries, len(RETRY_AFTER)) - 1] if slot.tries else 0
796	        if delay <= 0:
797	            self.request_sync((number,), why="not in sync yet")
798	            return
799	        # Charged a try: wait a while before the next.
800	        _LOGGER.debug(
801	            "%s slot %s: retry in %.0f s (tries %s)",
802	            self.name,
803	            number,
804	            delay,
805	            slot.tries,
806	        )
807	        slot.not_before = self.clock() + delay
808	
809	    async def _exchange(
810	        self,
811	        call: Callable[[], Awaitable[Any]],
812	        *,
813	        op: str,
814	        mark: int | None = None,
815	        slots: tuple[int, ...] = (),
816	        pay: bool = True,
817	        count: bool = True,
818	    ) -> Any:
819	        """
820	        Run one exchange after the gap, within the budget.
821	
822	        ``_sent`` is when it was sent, after the gap: reports on ``mark``
823	        taken in before then are dropped.
824	
825	        No answer -- the budget running out, a ``NO_ANSWER``, a transient
826	        failure that never left for the lock, or a network error -- counts
827	        against the lock. Any other ``LockError`` that was sent is the lock
828	        answering, refusals included. One that never left (the integration
829	        refusing) and anything else a provider raises (a bug in it, logged)
830	        say nothing about the lock: a bug is a transient failure charged to
831	        the slot it hits -- or, on a probe, no answer, so probing goes on.
832	        ``count`` off: no answer is not counted against the lock either.
833	        ``op`` and ``slots`` (``mark`` if not given) are only for the logs.
834	        """
835	        missed = self._no_answer if count else lambda: None
836	        where = _where(mark, slots)
837	        await self._pace(op, where)
838	        self._sent = self._next()
839	        if mark is not None:
840	            self._written[mark] = self._sent
841	            self._write_sent[mark] = time.monotonic()
842	        _LOGGER.debug("%s slot %s: %s exchange start", self.name, where, op)
843	        start = time.monotonic()
844	        outcome, detail = "answered", ""
845	        try:
846	            async with asyncio.timeout(self.budget):
847	                result = await call()
848	        except LockError as err:
849	            detail = err.kind.value
850	            if err.kind is ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER or (
851	                not err.sent and err.kind is ErrorKind.TRANSIENT
852	            ):
853	                outcome = "no answer"
854	                missed()
855	            elif err.sent:
856	                outcome = "refused"
857	                self._answer()
858	                self._pay()
859	            else:
860	                outcome = "not sent"
861	                if self._down_until is not None:
862	                    # The integration refusing, unsent: the slot is held for
863	                    # it, and it says nothing of the lock being back.
864	                    missed()
865	            raise
866	        except asyncio.CancelledError:
867	            outcome, detail = "no answer", "cancelled"
868	            if (task := asyncio.current_task()) is not None and task.cancelling():
869	                raise
870	            missed()
871	            raise LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, message="cancelled") from None
872	        except OSError as err:  # timeouts and dropped connections included
873	            outcome, detail = "no answer", type(err).__name__
874	            missed()
875	            raise LockError(
876	                ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, message=str(err) or "no answer"
877	            ) from err
878	        except Exception as err:
879	            outcome, detail = "failed", type(err).__name__
880	            _LOGGER.exception("Lock provider failed")
881	            self._bug = True
882	            if self._down_until is not None:
883	                missed()
884	            raise LockError(ErrorKind.TRANSIENT, message=str(err)) from err
885	        finally:
886	            self._last_exchange = self.clock()
887	            _LOGGER.debug(
888	                "%s slot %s: %s exchange %s in %.0f ms (%s)",
889	                self.name,
890	                where,
891	                op,
892	                outcome,
893	                _ms(start),
894	                detail,
895	            )
896	        self._answer()
897	        if pay:
898	            self._pay()
899	        return result
900	
901	    async def _pace(self, op: str, where: Any) -> None:
902	        """Wait out the gap since the last exchange; ``op``, ``where`` for the logs."""
903	        if self._last_exchange is not None:
904	            wait = self._last_exchange + self.gap - self.clock()
905	            if wait > 0:
906	                _LOGGER.debug(
907	                    "%s slot %s: %s waiting %.0f ms for the gap",
908	                    self.name,
909	                    where,
910	                    op,
911	                    wait * 1000,
912	                )
913	                await self.sleep(wait)
914	
915	    def _answer(self) -> None:
916	        was_down = self._down_until is not None
917	        self._answers += 1
918	        self._charged.clear()
919	        self._probed.clear()
920	        self._no_answers = 0
921	        self._down_until = None
922	        if was_down:
923	            # Back -- maybe by a probe from outside (the hard refresh): the
924	            # old backoff's probe would hold up the next outage's probes.
925	            self._probe_at = None
926	            # Every slot dropped while backing off is synced again.
927	            self.request_sync(why="lock back")
928	
929	    def _due(self) -> list[tuple[int, Slot]]:
930	        """Take the owed tries: the lock answered, so they were the slots'."""
931	        owed, self._owed = self._owed, {}
932	        return [
933	            (number, owing)
934	            for number, (owing, epoch) in owed.items()
935	            if owing.epoch == epoch and self._failed(owing)
936	        ]
937	
938	    def _pay(self, due: list[tuple[int, Slot]] | None = None) -> None:
939	        """Charge owed tries still failing once the answer's reading is in."""
940	        for number, slot in self._due() if due is None else due:
941	            if self._failed(slot):
942	                self._charge(number, slot)
943	
944	    def _no_answer(self) -> None:
945	        self._no_answers += 1
946	        if self._no_answers < BACKOFF_AFTER or self._stopping:
947	            return
948	        delay = min(
949	            BACKOFF_MIN * 2 ** min(self._no_answers - BACKOFF_AFTER, 16), BACKOFF_MAX
950	        )
951	        self._down_until = self.clock() + delay
952	        if self._probe_at is None:
953	            self._probe_at = self._down_until
954	
955	    def _probe(self) -> None:
956	        """
957	        Read one slot, the backoff over; an answer brings the lock back.
958	
959	        Each probe reads the next slot not held in turn -- every slot in
960	        turn once those have all gone unanswered since the lock last
961	        answered -- so a slot the lock ignores cannot keep it down for long;
962	        a provider bug on one is no answer. With no slot to read, the probe
963	        stays due: the next slot wanted starts the probing.
964	        """
965	        free = sorted(n for n, slot in self.slots.items() if slot.hold is None)
966	        if numbers := free if set(free) - self._probed else sorted(self.slots):
967	            self._probe_at = None
968	            self._probes += 1
969	            number = numbers[self._probes % len(numbers)]
970	            self._probed.add(number)
971	            self._put(_Job("probe", slots=(number,)), "backoff probe")
